title: WASSCE Further Maths: Calculus (Differentiation & Integration) - Further Mathematics - Indefinite Integrals
subject: Further Mathematics

questions.explain: Integrate each term using the power rule $\int x^n dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C$. $\int 4x^3 dx = x^4$ and $\int -6x dx = -3x^2$. Adding the constant of integration yields $x^4 - 3x^2 + C$.
questions.subject: Further Mathematics

questions.q: Evaluate the indefinite integral $\int e^{2x} dx$.
questions.explain: The general rule for integrating an exponential function $e^{kx}$ is $\frac{1}{k}e^{kx} + C$. Here $k = 2$, so the integral is $\frac{1}{2}e^{2x} + C$.
questions.subject: Further Mathematics

questions.explain: Apply the power rule for integration $\int x^n dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C$. $\int 2x^{-3} dx = 2 \left( \frac{x^{-2}}{-2} \right) + C = -x^{-2} + C$.
questions.subject: Further Mathematics

questions.explain: Using the standard integration rule $\int \frac{1}{x} dx = \ln|x| + C$, factoring out the constant 3 yields $3 \int \frac{1}{x} dx = 3\ln|x| + C$.
